To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human neuroblastoma cells SH-SY5y and SK-N-SY express the insulin-like growth factor II (IGF-II), IGF-I and IGF receptor type I and type II mRNA transcripts.
the human neuroblastoma cells lines SH-SY5 Y and SK-N-S H express multiple transcripts of the IGF II gene, as well as the type I and type II IGF receptors.
1) The human neuroblastoma lines SH-SY5y and SK-N-Sy have been established as good in vitro model systems for the investigation of the role of IGF in the development of the nervous system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate gene expression in the nervous system, with particular reference to the insulin-like growth factor (IGF) family of growth factors.
the regulation of the insulin-like and growth factors (IGFs) during nervous system development.
the regulation of insulin-like growth factors ( IGF ) and their receptors during human fetal development, with an emphasis on the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IGFs and their receptors play a significant role in the development of the human central nervous system.
the IGF system has an important role in the growth and development of the central nervous system.
IGF-II is a growth factor which plays a role in the development and differentiation of neuronal cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of IGF and IGR mRNAs in the neuroblastoma cell line SH-SY5y is similar to the developmental profile of IGF and IR expression found during normal human development.
IGF-I is a potent growth factor for neuroblastoma cell proliferation and survival and that it may be important for neuroblastoma growth and differentiation in vivo.
IGF II and IGF I mRNA are present in human neuroblastomas and the expression of the mRNA is developmentally regulated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neuroblastoma cell line, SH-SY 5Y, can be used as a model to understand the role of IGF in the development of nervous system and also in the development of neuroblastoma.
the expression patterns of these IGF and IGH receptor transcripts in these neuroblastoma cell line are very similar to those seen during development of the human nervous system.
